info.name: Mesh Connect Integration Headless Bridging API
info.description:
Mesh allows users to connect accounts of financial institutions,
crypto exchanges, and self-custody wallets. Mesh handles credential
validation, MFA, and error handling for each integration. After
an account is connected, Mesh allows client applications to read holdings,
transaction history and balances and execute crypto transfers (with user approval).

item.name: Discover pay-in (source) bridging routes for one or more payout destinations

request.description:
Networks and assets use CAIP-2 + token symbol.
Use `optimized` to collapse to one destination per distinct source (default) or return every matching origin→destination pair.

response.name: Routes retrieved successfully. An empty `routes` array means no routes are currently available for the given destinations.

item.name: Discover payout (destination) bridging routes for fixed omnibus (source) legs

request.description:
Provide at least one `sources` entry (CAIP-2 network + asset). When `optimized` is `true` (default),
returns at most one source per distinct destination. Set `optimized` to `false`
to list every matching origin→destination pair for those sources.

response.name: Routes retrieved successfully. An empty `routes` array means no routes are currently available for the given sources.

item.name: Create a one-time bridging deposit address for a selected origin→destination…

request.description:
Returns a single-use address on the origin network for the origin asset. Funds must be
sent to that address on that chain; Mesh detects the deposit, executes the bridge, and delivers
to `destination.address` on the destination network.

**Deposit-style (user pay-in):** discover routes with `POST /api/v1/bridging/routes/deposit`.
The end user sends from their wallet to the returned deposit address.

**Withdrawal-style (platform pay-in):** discover routes with `POST /api/v1/bridging/routes/withdrawal`
to pair an omnibus `origin` with the user’s chosen destination. Your platform sends the origin
asset from that omnibus wallet to the deposit address; the user’s withdrawal address is `destination.address`.

**Idempotency:** a `transactionId` is single-use per `userId`. While the transfer is still
pending, re-submitting the same `transactionId` + `userId` with the same origin, destination and
address returns the previously created address unchanged (same `transferId`, same
`expirationTime`) rather than generating a new one, so network-error retries are safe. Re-submitting
with a different origin, destination or address is a `400`. Once the transfer has reached a terminal
state (succeeded, failed or expired), the same `transactionId` returns `409`; use a new
`transactionId` for a new address.

**Expiry:** `constraints.expirationTime` is fixed at creation (6 hours by default) and is the point at
which Mesh stops tracking the address. A transfer that has not been funded by then is marked failed; a
pay-in that arrives before then is bridged and the transfer moves to succeeded as soon as it settles. Do
not display or use the address after `expirationTime`: the provider may still bridge funds sent
later, but Mesh will not track them automatically.

**Minimum amount:** `constraints.minimumAmount` is the smallest pay-in (in the origin asset) Mesh
accepts on this route: the stricter of the route's configured minimum and the platform USD floor
converted at the current price. It is the same value `POST /api/v1/bridging/quote` returns in its
`constraints` and enforces with `amountBelowMinimum`. `constraints.maximumAmount` is the
platform USD cap converted at the current price (enforced on `/quote` with `amountExceedsMaximum`);
the provider's available liquidity may be lower and surfaces at quote time the same way.

**Typical flow:**
1. Discover routes (`routes/deposit` or `routes/withdrawal`) and fix `origin` + `destination`
(destination includes the recipient withdrawal address when applicable).
2. Call this endpoint with those values.
3. Show the deposit address, constraints (`minimumAmount`, `expirationTime`, `singleUseAddress`),
and warnings to whoever will broadcast the pay-in (end user or your custody system).
4. After the pay-in is sent on-chain, Mesh completes the bridge to the destination address.
5. Use `transferId` from `tracking` for webhooks or the transfer status API.

**Important:** the deposit address is single-use; do not reuse it.

response.name: Bridging deposit address created or retrieved (idempotent hit).

item.name: Get an indicative quote for bridging a given pay-in amount on a configured…

request.description:
Stateless: no deposit address is minted and no transfer is created. Use this while the end user is
choosing an amount, then call `POST /api/v1/bridging/address` once they confirm.

`amount` is denominated in the `origin` asset (what will be sent to the deposit address).
The response returns `destination.estimatedAmount` (net of provider fees), `destination.minimumAmount`
(the provider's indicative minimum for this quote at the configured slippage, when reported), and the fee
lines that produced the estimate. The quote is not bound to a later `/address` call, which obtains a
fresh quote that may differ.

`constraints.minimumAmount` is the smallest pay-in Mesh accepts on this route (in the origin asset);
an `amount` below it is rejected with `400 amountBelowMinimum` before the provider is consulted,
and the same value is returned by `POST /api/v1/bridging/address`. `constraints.maximumAmount` is
the platform USD cap converted at the current price; an amount above it, or above the provider's available
liquidity, is rejected with `400 amountExceedsMaximum`.

**Important:** the estimate is indicative. The deposit address accepts any amount and the bridge is
priced on what actually arrives, so fees and rates can move between quoting and settlement.
